inputs.original_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to complete renegotiations of the 2009 agreement with non-teaching university unions, or face an indefinite nationwide strike. Workers should not have to threaten a shutdown to make institutions honor commitments they have left unresolved for years. Universities depend on non-teaching staff, yet their labor and livelihoods are too easily treated as secondary. The government needs to negotiate seriously and deliver fair treatment—not wait for workers to withdraw their labor before listening.
inputs.modified_text: SSANU has given the federal government one month to finish renegotiating the 2009 agreement or face an indefinite nationwide strike. The fact that workers must threaten to withdraw their labor just to get long-unresolved commitments taken seriously shows the imbalance: universities rely on non-teaching staff, while their work and livelihoods are treated as expendable. This is not a failure of workers to be patient; it is a failure of institutions to honor their obligations. The government should negotiate seriously and deliver fair treatment before workers are forced to shut things down.
